cards.text: Saul, Israel’s king, has been chasing David for a while now, and David already let him go once, in a cave (1 Samuel 24). Now the Ziphites, people from around Ziph, show up at Saul’s place in Gibeah with a tip. Isn’t David hiding on the hill of Hachilah, opposite Jeshimon?

cards.question: Saul goes down to the Wilderness of Ziph to search for David, and he takes ___ chosen men of Israel with him.

cards.text: Three THOUSAND men. To find ONE guy. On ONE hill. Saul camps beside the road at Hachilah, and out in the wilderness, David realizes Saul has followed him there.

cards.question: Before he makes a move, David sends out spies to make sure Saul has really arrived.

cards.text: Most people run AWAY from three thousand soldiers, but David heads straight for the camp to take a look. He spots where Saul has lain down, along with Abner son of Ner, the general of Saul’s army.

cards.question: With three thousand troops in Saul’s camp, where is the king himself lying down?

answers.text: Inside the inner circle of the camp
Out at the far edge of the camp
Off by himself up on the hill

cards.text: David turns to Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, and asks who will go down with him to Saul in the camp. Friend, into a camp of three thousand soldiers? That’s not a question. That’s a DARE.

cards.question: David asks Ahimelech and Abishai who will go down with him into Saul’s camp. Who says yes?

cards.text: That night David and Abishai come right up to the troops, and there’s Saul, asleep in the inner circle, with his spear stuck in the ground by his head. Abner and the troops are lying all around him, and David just… walks up.

cards.question: Abishai is standing over the sleeping king, with Saul’s own spear right there. What does Abishai want to do?

answers.text: Pin Saul to the ground with the spear
Tie Saul up and carry him off
Wake Saul up and make him surrender

cards.text: Abishai says, “Today God has delivered your enemy into your hand.” He asks David to let him do it in one stroke, no second try needed, and friend, back when my edges were worn down, I never stamped ANYTHING that confidently.

cards.question: Abishai is ready to strike. Why does David tell him not to destroy Saul?

cards.text: David adds that the LORD Himself will strike Saul down. Either Saul’s day will come and he’ll die, or he’ll go into battle and perish.

cards.question: David tells Abishai to leave everything by Saul’s head untouched and just walk away.
David tells Abishai, “Instead, take the ___ and water jug by his head, and let us go.”
As David and Abishai leave with the spear and water jug, nobody in Saul’s camp wakes up, because a deep sleep from the LORD has fallen on them.

cards.text: In and out with the king’s own spear and water jug, and no one saw them or knew about it. Three thousand men, and not ONE of them so much as rolled over.

David crosses to the other side and stands on top of the mountain, way off in the distance, with a wide gulf between them. Smart man. If you’re about to yell at three thousand soldiers, you do it from ACROSS a gulf.

cards.question: From across the gulf, the first one David shouts to is Saul himself.

cards.text: David shouts to the troops and to Abner, and Abner calls back, “Who are you who calls to the king?” Then David starts in on him: you’re a man, aren’t you, and who in Israel is your equal?

cards.question: David says nobody in Israel is Abner’s equal. So what does David want to know from Abner?

answers.text: Why he didn’t protect the king
Why he’s chasing an innocent man
Why he came into the wilderness

cards.text: David says what Abner has done is not good, and all of them deserve to die for not protecting the LORD’s anointed. Then comes the line I use every time my sprinkles go missing: “Now look around.”

cards.question: David asks Abner where the king’s ___ and water ___ are, the ones that were by his head.
Over in Saul’s camp, Abner is the one who recognizes David’s voice.

cards.text: Saul calls out, “Is that your voice, David my son?” David answers, “It is my voice, my lord and king,” and friend, that’s the politest hello ever shouted across a gulf to three thousand soldiers.

cards.question: Saul and David are finally talking. What does David ask the king?

answers.text: Will you make me your general
Can I come back to Gibeah

cards.text: What has he done, David asks, and what evil is in his hand? If the LORD stirred Saul up against him, may He accept an offering, but if men did it, may they be cursed in the presence of the LORD.

cards.question: David says the men who stirred Saul up have driven him away, telling him to go serve other gods. Driven him away from sharing in what?
David asks Saul not to let his blood fall far from the presence of the LORD. Then he says the king of Israel has come out, like someone hunting a partridge in the mountains, to look for what?
Saul hears David out and refuses to admit he’s done anything wrong.

cards.text: Saul answers, “I have sinned. Come back, David my son.” He says he’ll never harm David again, and then, “I have played the fool and have committed a grave error!” Friend, I said almost that exact line the day I put in a whole batch and forgot the timer.

cards.question: David crosses back over the gulf and hands Saul’s spear back to him himself.

cards.text: “Here is the king’s spear,” David answers, and he tells Saul to let one of the young men come over and get it. Then David says the LORD delivered Saul into his hand today, but he would not extend his hand against the LORD’s anointed.

cards.question: David says, “As surely as I valued your life today, so may the ___ value my life and rescue me from all trouble.”

cards.text: Saul says to him, “May you be blessed, David my son. You will accomplish great things and will surely prevail.” That’s a LONG way from three thousand soldiers, friend.

cards.question: After Saul blesses David, where do the two of them go?

answers.text: David leaves and Saul goes home

cards.text: Two men, two different roads, and that’s where we’ll leave them for now. But trust me, friend, this story is NOT done.
